2025.clinched: Petit Le Mans, Road Atlanta, 11 October 2025, final round
2025.note: Campbell and Jaminet finished third in the Petit Le Mans finale on 11 October 2025 and that settled it, in a #6 Porsche shared with Laurens Vanthoor, who was driving both factory 963s after Julien Andlauer withdrew with back pain. The two champions nearly missed the start: stuck in more than ninety minutes of traffic outside a record crowd, they abandoned their car and walked, and the team sent a golf cart to collect them. The #31 Cadillac of Jack Aitken, Earl Bamber and Frederik Vesti won the race. They had finished outside the top five only once all season.

2024.clinched: Petit Le Mans, Road Atlanta, 12 October 2024, final round
2024.note: Cameron and Nasr took the title with third place in the Petit Le Mans finale on 12 October 2024, having built their margin partly in the stewards' room: at Indianapolis the sister #6 Porsche lost its result when a wiring harness was found to be outside homologation, which turned a fourteen-point gap into 124. Both Porsche Penske cars led for long stretches of the ten hours and were beaten in the final sprint by a Cadillac. Porsche locked out the top two places in the teams' standings and took the manufacturers' title as well.

2023.clinched: Petit Le Mans, Road Atlanta, 14 October 2023, final round
2023.note: Six crews, one from each of the four GTP manufacturers, could still win the championship at Road Atlanta on 14 October 2023, and Derani and Sims led it by three points. Sixth place settled it, by 21. With an hour left Derani and Filipe Albuquerque were fighting over second place and the title when Albuquerque went for the outside of turn one and ended up on the grass, spearing his Acura into the tyre barriers; the stewards took no action. The #31 won only once all year, at Sebring. Meyer Shank's Acura won the race, in its last start before a hiatus.

2022.clinched: Petit Le Mans, Road Atlanta, 1 October 2022, final round
2022.note: Blomqvist and Jarvis only had to finish ahead of Ricky Taylor and Filipe Albuquerque, and won the race instead. Albuquerque was leading when a caution fell for a crash at turn one with 51 minutes to go; both Acuras pitted, Meyer Shank's stop was the cleaner one and released Blomqvist into the lead, and the #10 then hit a lapped car with fourteen minutes left and lost its rear suspension. The margin was six points over Wayne Taylor Racing, built on five consecutive second places in mid-season. They were the last DPi champions: the class ended that day.

2021.clinched: Petit Le Mans, Road Atlanta, 13 November 2021, final round
2021.note: Nasr and Derani went to Road Atlanta eight points behind Ricky Taylor and Filipe Albuquerque, took pole for the maximum qualifying points, and reduced the championship to a straight fight over which of the two cars finished ahead. On the last lap Taylor went for the inside of Turn 10A, the two touched, the Acura bounced through a gravel trap and rejoined in front, and Nasr still took second by 0.405 seconds. Mazda won the race in its final DPi start. It was Action Express Racing's fifth prototype teams' title since 2014.

2020.clinched: 12 Hours of Sebring, 14 November 2020, final round
2020.note: The pandemic pushed the 2020 finale to Sebring in November, and Castroneves and Taylor won the championship there by a single point after the worst possible afternoon. Forty minutes in, the left intercooler on the #7 Acura failed and a 25-minute repair dropped them twelve laps down; with Alexander Rossi sharing the car they climbed back to eighth, which was exactly enough. They had arrived two points ahead of the #10 Cadillac and nine ahead of Pipo Derani. Mazda won the race. Acura took all six major titles across the prototype and GT Daytona classes that season.

2019.clinched: Petit Le Mans, Road Atlanta, 12 October 2019, final round
2019.note: Cameron and Montoya needed eighth place at Road Atlanta on 12 October 2019 and finished fourth, after a caution inside the last half hour bunched the field and Montoya gained places in the sprint to the flag. The #31 Cadillac of Felipe Nasr, Pipo Derani and Eric Curran won the race, and Nasr and Derani were the pair they had beaten to the championship. Three wins and a run of seven consecutive podiums did it. It was Montoya's first IMSA title, Cameron's second in prototypes, and Team Penske's eleventh in sports cars.

2018.clinched: Petit Le Mans, Road Atlanta, October 2018, final round
2018.note: Curran and Nasr arrived at Road Atlanta four points ahead of Jon Bennett and Colin Braun, with four more crews still mathematically alive, and took the championship on 277 points. Their season was one win, at Detroit, and five podiums in ten races: the #31 Whelen Cadillac scored steadily and let the others lose it. Action Express also sealed a fifth consecutive North American Endurance Cup, confirmed when Nasr was scored as the leader at the four-hour mark. Wayne Taylor Racing won the race. It was a second prototype title for Curran and a first in the series for Nasr.

2017.clinched: Petit Le Mans, Road Atlanta, 7 October 2017, final round (10 of 10)
2017.note: The Taylor brothers won the 2017 championship on a day their car barely ran. The #10 Cadillac started seventh and finished ninth with a mechanical problem, completing 97 of the race's 402 laps on 7 October 2017, and none of it mattered: five wins to open the season, at Daytona, Sebring, Long Beach, Austin and Detroit, had built a lead of 19 points that Road Atlanta could not touch. They ended on 310. Extreme Speed Motorsports won the race. Ricky Taylor left his father's team for Acura Team Penske the following season.

2016.clinched: Petit Le Mans, Road Atlanta, 1 October 2016, final round (12 of 12)
2016.note: Cameron and Curran led the championship by a single point going into the finale, 286 to 285, and the crew behind them were their own Action Express team-mates and the two-time defending champions, João Barbosa and Christian Fittipaldi. They finished the season on 314 points, three clear. Two wins, at Canadian Tire Motorsport Park and Road America, and seven podiums from ten races carried it. Michael Shank Racing won the race on the eve of its 250th and final prototype start. It was the last season for the Daytona Prototypes.

2015.clinched: Petit Le Mans, Road Atlanta, 3 October 2015, final round
2015.note: Barbosa and Fittipaldi were six points behind Michael Valiante and Richard Westbrook going into a Petit Le Mans that the weather cut short at seven hours and fifty-one minutes, and they won the Prototype class in it, with Sébastien Bourdais sharing the car, to take a second consecutive title. Their own team-mates Dane Cameron and Eric Curran had been tied with them on points and were running an off-strategy race that had worked perfectly until the last caution fell just after they pitted. Barbosa said afterwards that it was unfortunate to decide a championship that way.

2014.clinched: Petit Le Mans, Road Atlanta, 4 October 2014, final round
2014.note: The first champions of the unified series, formed that year out of the merger of the American Le Mans Series and Grand-Am. Barbosa and Fittipaldi needed second place at Road Atlanta on 4 October 2014 and got it, eleven seconds behind Jordan Taylor, who took the lead with about ninety minutes left and held it through a late caution to complete a Corvette one-two. Jordan and Ricky Taylor were the first American drivers to win Petit Le Mans outright. The #5 Action Express car completed every mile of the season, and had won the Rolex 24 to open it.
